## Find amino acid associated to codon using `find_aa()`

The `find_aa()` function translates an RNA codon into its corresponding amino acid using the package's codon_table lookup table. It accepts one or more codons as input and returns the associated amino acid abbreviations as a character string.

Examples

```{r}
find_aa(codons = "UUU")
```

The codon UUU encodes phenylalanine, represented by the one-letter abbreviation F.

The function can also accept multiple codons:

```{r}
find_aa(codons = c("UUU", "AUG", "GGU"))
```

Here, UUU encodes phenylalanine (F), AUG encodes methionine (M), and GGU encodes glycine (G). The function concatenates the results into a single character string.

`find_aa()` can be used to translate codons obtained from an RNA sequence-processing function, allowing users to convert codon data into amino acid representations.
